threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You’re still using a plastic umbrella; locals know a proper Hackney day demands a sturdy one, or you'll be left wet and sorry.
Last night on the 77, a guy sat beside me singing elevator music to himself. Honestly, it was oddly calming amid the chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the spontaneous street party outside my window turned into an impromptu dance-off, and I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 4 AM and then stumble into a techno party in a backroom café where the vibe's somehow both chaotic and cozy.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know to avoid the BART station when it’s foggy; the tourists always think it's just a light drizzle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy practicing stand-up on the 19 Polk. Front row was a packed crowd, he had them laughing about the Muni delays. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think tapas are a snack, but for us, it’s a whole evening ritual—pa amb tomàquet and vermut, without a rush.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still use the 'V' in 'Barcelona' instead of just 'Barna' when chatting with locals.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Broadway Market' instead of just 'the Market.' It’s a sure sign you haven't yet been swept up in the weekend hustle.
Last night on the 35, heard a couple argue over whose turn it was to pay for chips. Lively debate, but the bus driver just chuckled.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a guy selling fresh simit on a street corner, chatting with the old lady about her garden. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous techno parties in the U-Bahn tunnels at midnight, complete with DJs and a surprisingly cozy vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their ability to navigate BART delays without breaking a sweat—while newcomers just stare at the screen, confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I saw a guy on the 27 line juggling for tips while a woman sang opera. Only in SF do you get a full concert during your morning commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab a 'café con leche' and rush out, but locals actually linger in the plazas, sipping slowly, enjoying the vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overzealous Instagram posts from Plaça del Sol, as if no one’s ever seen a terrace before.
